# Your First Java Program

#### Course: Learn Java Basics

## Your First Java Program

To get a feel of what Java code looks like, let's write our first Java program.

We'll write a simple program that displays Hello, World! on the screen.

```java
1class Main {
2    public static void main(String[] args) {
3
4        System.out.println("Hello, World!");
5    }
6}
```

Don't worry about the code. For now, just press the Run Code button to run the program.

If you get Hello, World! as output, congratulations! You've successfully run your first Java program.

Next, let's learn how this code works.

##### How does it work?

Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.

##### Common questions people ask:

Molly Lindsay

##### what does args mean?

![User profile picture](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

Abhilekh Gautam from Programiz

Great question!

In the line public static void main(String[] args), args is short for arguments. It’s used to pass information into your program when it starts. For example, if you wanted to give your program some input when running it, args would hold that information.

But don’t worry about it too much right now! You’ll learn more about args and how to use it in later lessons.

For now, just focus on running your program and seeing "Hello, World!" appear. Keep up the great work!

##### why do we need to write public static void

![User profile picture](data:image/png;base64,)

Udayan Shakya from Programiz

Hello, there! You'll learn about the significance of public static when you learn about object-oriented programming in our Java OOP course.

As for void, you'll learn what it means in the Methods chapter of the current course.

As you can see, these topics will be explored in due time. For now, just know that this is how Java programs are written.

So please be patient and continue with your lessons. As a beginner, your first priority is to grasp the basics.

That being said, you're always welcome to ask new questions whenever you get stuck. We're always here to help!
